page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features an expansive 480 MB L3 cache, complemented by 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. It integrates hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE and AMX-INT8) for dense matrix computation.

System memory consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage, relying instead on network-attached remote storage configurations with Premium Storage support. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included. Benchmark measurements show strong results across cached memory read bandwidth reaching 3,768.18 GB/sec, alongside top-tier single-threaded compression performance with gzip at 36.88 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.37 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory throughput drops into average tiers at 176.07 GB/sec read and 69.43 GB/sec write.

Compute benchmarks highlight robust throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,335.0, a Passmark CPU score of 68,640.57, and strong compilation metrics in Clang at 46,329.0. In-memory data store performance is demonstrated by Redis SET throughput reaching 83.69 million operations per second. Hardware matrix extensions provide viable CPU-based inference capability, processing 3,667.57 tokens per second on small 135M language models and 258.1 tokens per second on 7B models during prompt evaluation.

The D48s_v7 delivers balanced compute and memory capacity for enterprise workloads requiring sustained CPU throughput without dedicated graphics accelerators. Its configuration is matched to high-concurrency web serving, large relational and NoSQL database hosting, continuous integration build clusters, and CPU-driven batch processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor at 4.2 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 24 physical cores with two threads per core and a 480 MB L3 cache, alongside AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing external Premium Storage for disk needs. Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-threaded decompression and compression rates, strong multi-core Clang compilation, and high in-memory Redis processing at 83.69 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth scales efficiently for small cached blocks, while CPU-based machine learning inference handles small to medium models effectively. The instance is designed for high-throughput enterprise databases, large-scale build pipelines, static web delivery, and distributed data processing tasks.
